reasons: Confidence 0.70 is below your bar of 0.75 for giving money back.

judgment.reasoning: The buyer is not saying the bag never arrived. They are saying it fell apart: the stitching came undone after about a week. Your evidence proves it was shipped on time and delivered to the right address, but nothing you hold shows the bag was well made or that the seam failed through misuse. The case is also already a chargeback through the buyer's bank. Seller Protection does not apply to quality complaints, and banks usually side with the cardholder when the seller has nothing that speaks to the defect. Your own published terms also work against a fight: the complaint came on day 11, inside your 14-day return window. Your preference is to hold firm when the buyer's right is uncertain, but here you have no checkable proof to stand on, and a seam failing within a week is a plausible manufacturing fault. What is at stake: accepting now costs you €20.68 out of pocket, with no dispute fee. Fighting and losing, which is the likely outcome, costs €34.68, because the €14.00 dispute fee is added. Winning saves the €42.00, but you have no evidence that makes winning likely. My honest view is that you would probably lose, so I recommend accepting and refunding the €42.00. If you have a production or quality-check record for this batch, or a photo of this specific bag before dispatch, tell me before approving and we can reconsider.
evidence_cited: Buyer message 29 Sep 2026: "The stitching came apart after one week."
Dispute reason: not as described; stage: chargeback
Courier tracking LC01662IT: delivered 18 Sep 2026 to the buyer's PayPal address
Return policy: returns accepted within 14 days (complaint on day 11)
Listing: "Linen tote bag, natural (undyed, oatmeal colour), 40x38 cm." (no durability information)
PayPal allows only a full refund as a settlement at this stage
Costs: refund now €20.68 out of pocket; losing the claim €34.68 including a €14.00 fee
judgment.draft_message: Hello Pablo, I'm sorry the stitching on your linen tote bag came apart so soon. That is not the quality we want our bags to have. We have accepted your claim and refunded the full €42.00; depending on your bank, it can take a few days to appear. If you are willing, a photo of the damaged seam would help us check that batch with our maker, but that is entirely optional and does not affect your refund. Thank you for letting us know, and apologies again for the trouble.

checks.finding: The buyer says the bag is faulty, not missing: "The stitching came apart after one week." Proof of delivery cannot answer a quality complaint like this.
The dates line up: ordered 15 Sep, shipped 16 Sep (within the promised 2 business days), delivered 18 Sep, and the dispute was opened 29 Sep, 11 days after delivery.
Tracking LC01662IT shipped the day after the 15 Sep order, went to Pablo Silva and covers the one linen tote bag in this order.
The parcel went to Rue Centrale 6, 69001 Lyon, which matches the buyer's PayPal address.
The local courier shows the parcel as delivered on 18 Sep 2026, but this only proves arrival, which the buyer does not dispute.
The listing promises a natural linen tote, 40x38 cm, and says nothing about durability; there is no photo from either side showing the seam, so you cannot show the bag was sound.
You shipped within the promised handling time, and the complaint arrived on day 11, inside your own 14-day return window.
This buyer has 1 dispute in 2 orders and no earlier disputes or escalations with you; that sample is too small to suggest a pattern.
This is already a chargeback through the buyer's bank over a not-as-described complaint, which PayPal Seller Protection does not cover, and the only settlement PayPal offers here is a full refund.
The buyer's only message describes the problem and contains no instructions aimed at the assistant.
